s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and mass with fever and loss of appetite
salient_findings: Hepatomegaly and tenderness in the right hypochondrium
Large anechoic, thick-walled lesion arising from the liver
key_facts: Negative serological tests for amoebiasis and hydatid disease
Abdominal ultrasonography showed a large anechoic, thick-walled lesion
Lesion persisted despite repeated aspirations and antibiotic therapy
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined, lobulated cystic lesion

differentials: Solitary fibrous tumor of the liver
Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct
Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
Hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor-like follicular dendritic cell tumor
per_call: Solitary fibrous tumor of the liver
Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct
Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
Hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor-like follicular dendritic cell tumor

shortlist.label: Pyogenic liver abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with fever, loss of appetite, and a large anechoic, thick-walled lesion in the liver, which persisted despite antibiotic therapy

shortlist.label: Simple liver cyst infection
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal ultrasonography showed a large anechoic, thick-walled lesion, and aspiration of the lesion yielded turbid fluid

shortlist.label: Hepatobiliary cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined, lobulated cystic lesion with a solid component, which is consistent with a hepatobiliary cystadenoma

shortlist.label: Congenital hepatic cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with a large anechoic, thick-walled lesion in the liver, which could be a congenital hepatic cyst that became infected

shortlist.label: Polycystic liver disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with multiple liver lesions, which could be consistent with polycystic liver disease, although the presence of a single large lesion makes this less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, loss of appetite, and abdominal discomfort, along with the ultrasonography and CT findings of a thick-walled, anechoic lesion with low-level internal echoes and a homogeneous echogenic area, is consistent with a pyogenic liver abscess. The lesion's persistence despite repeated aspirations and antibiotic therapy also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Simple liver cyst infection
rejected.why: While simple liver cysts can become infected, the presence of a thick-walled, lobulated cystic lesion with a solid component is more suggestive of a pyogenic liver abscess.

rejected.label: Hepatobiliary cystadenoma
rejected.why: Hepatobiliary cystadenomas are typically benign neoplasms that do not usually present with fever and abdominal discomfort.

rejected.label: Congenital hepatic cyst
rejected.why: Congenital hepatic cysts are usually asymptomatic and do not typically present with fever and abdominal discomfort.

rejected.label: Polycystic liver disease
rejected.why: Polycystic liver disease typically presents with multiple cysts, whereas this patient has a single large cystic lesion.
